Kururin Squash! is a puzzle video game developed by Eighting and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo GameCube, released exclusively in Japan on October 14, 2004. The game features a character named Kururin, who navigates through mazes, collecting coins and avoiding enemies. It introduces a variety of new items and obstacles, including water levels with a submarine, guns, boxing gloves, twisters, flame-throwing, and boss battles.

In Kururin Squash!, the player controls Kururin, a constantly rotating stick, as they navigate through mazes to reach the goal without hitting any obstacles. The game introduces a new mechanic where players can collect coins, enemies, and bosses, each with their own unique challenges. Water levels feature a submarine, and there are also levels where players can use guns, boxing gloves, twisters, flame-throwing, and engage in boss battles.

Kururin Squash! is the third and final game in the Kururin series. It follows the original game, Kuru Kuru Kururin, and its sequel, Kururin Paradise, both of which were released in Japan only. The game was developed by Eighting and published by Nintendo for the GameCube platform.

Kururin Squash! received a mixed reception from critics. The game was praised for its innovative mechanics and engaging gameplay, but it was also criticized for its limited scope and lack of variety. While it was not a commercial success, it still holds a place in the puzzle game genre.

Kururin Squash! is a puzzle video game that adds new elements to the series, including water levels, guns, boxing gloves, and boss battles. The game was well-received for its innovative gameplay but faced criticism for its limited scope. It remains a notable entry in the Kururin series and the Nintendo GameCube library.

_Kururin Squash!_ is the third and final game in the Kururin series. It was released for the [GameCube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameCube) on October 14th, 2004. Unlike its predecessors, _Kururin Squash!_ has never been rereleased, and remains exclusive to the GameCube.

[![Image 1](https://static.wikitide.net/kururinwiki/f/f4/Kururin_Squash%21_Coverart.jpg)](https://kururin.miraheze.org/wiki/File:Kururin_Squash!_Coverart.jpg)

Coverart of Kururin Squash!

The story follows [Kururin](https://kururin.miraheze.org/wiki/Kururin "Kururin"), who was on a free family vacation his family won. However, when Kururin gets home, he notices all his siblings are gone. Professor Isogashima had captured them, and he built several robots to stop Kururin from "interfering with his research". After Kururin rescues all his siblings, he goes home, but his father, Totorin, is not there. Isogashima had kidnapped him in Wonderverse, the final level in the game. So Kururin rides the [Helirin](https://kururin.miraheze.org/wiki/Helirin "Helirin") to save him. Beatable "Dad" times on each level are unlocked after rescuing Totorin. Throughout the game, Teacher Hare invents new Helirins to help Kururin progress.

[![Image 2](https://static.wikitide.net/kururinwiki/thumb/c/c1/Why_are_you_catching_my_brothers%3F.png/300px-Why_are_you_catching_my_brothers%3F.png)](https://kururin.miraheze.org/wiki/File:Why_are_you_catching_my_brothers%3F.png)

A screenshot of the first cutscene of the NewGBAXL English translation patch of Kururin Squash!

The gameplay is similar to the prior 2 games. You control the [Helirin](https://kururin.miraheze.org/wiki/Helirin "Helirin"), an automatically spinning stick, through tight mazes. When Helirin hits the wall, you lose a heart. When you lose all 3 (5 if a Heart-Up is used) hearts, Helirin shatters and the level must be restarted, or, if an Amazing Heart is used, restart from the last heart panel. By pressing the B button, Helirin will move faster and by pressing the R button, Helirin will rotate faster. There are blue springs throughout the levels that will cause Helirin to rotate in the opposite direction it's currently rotating in. New to this game, are five Helirins, [Helibokaan](https://kururin.miraheze.org/wiki/Helibokaan "Helibokaan"), [Helibashan](https://kururin.miraheze.org/wiki/Helibashan "Helibashan"), [Heliboboh](https://kururin.miraheze.org/wiki/Heliboboh "Heliboboh"), [Heliburuun](https://kururin.miraheze.org/wiki/Heliburuun "Heliburuun"), and [Helibibyuun](https://kururin.miraheze.org/wiki/Helibibyuun "Helibibyuun"). The Helibokaan (Helibash in the NewGBAXL patch) is used in some levels in Sweet Shores. When the A button is pressed, the boxing gloves on both end of it will extend, and it will punch through obstacles and enemies, rewarding the player with coins. The Helibashan (Helibubble in the NewGBAXL patch) is used in some levels in Coastal Canopy. When the A button is pressed, Helibashan will go underwater until either the A button is released, or when air runs out. The Heliboboh (Heliblaze in the NewGBAXL patch) is used in some levels in Snowscape. When the A button is pressed, flames will released from either side, which will kill enemies. If you dash with the B button, the flames get longer. The Heliburuun (Heliblow in the NewGBAXL patch) is used in some levels in CyberCity. If you hold the A button long enough, when you let go, a tornado will be released that can kill enemies, reveal areas obscured by smoke, and block fire. The Helibibyuun (Helibeam in the NewGBAXL patch) is used in some levels in Wonderverse. When the A button is pressed, lasers will shoot out of either side of it. These lasers kill enemies and can shoot bombs. At the end of each world, you fight a boss with the Helirin used in that level.

[![Image 3](https://static.wikitide.net/kururinwiki/thumb/2/22/Sweet_Shores_4_Screenshot.png/300px-Sweet_Shores_4_Screenshot.png)](https://kururin.miraheze.org/wiki/File:Sweet_Shores_4_Screenshot.png)

A screenshot of the level Sweet Shores 4.

_**Kururin Squash!**_[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-2) is a 2004 [puzzle video game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puzzle_video_game "Puzzle video game") developed by [Eighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eighting "Eighting") and published by [Nintendo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo "Nintendo") for the [GameCube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameCube "GameCube"). It was released exclusively in Japan on October 14, 2004. _Kururin Squash!_ is the third and final game in the _Kururin_ series as well as the first entry on a home console, following the release of _[Kuru Kuru Kururin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuru\_Kuru\_Kururin "Kuru Kuru Kururin")_ (2001) and _[Kururin Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin\_Paradise "Kururin Paradise")_ (2002) on the [Game Boy Advance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy_Advance "Game Boy Advance"). The game uses [3D graphics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_computer_graphics "3D computer graphics"), with 2D artwork of its characters being used on cardboard cutouts outside of gameplay.

_Kururin Squash!_ is a maze navigation game where the player attempts to reach the goal at the end for a high score. It introduces coins, enemies, and bosses in its levels, with multiple new vehicles being used to overcome specific obstacles. _Kururin Squash!_ received generally positive reviews from critics for its gameplay, visuals, and style, with mixed opinions on its difficulty. It is considered to be one of the best Japanese-exclusive GameCube games. Selling less than 20,000 copies, it is the lowest-selling _Kururin_ game, and it is Nintendo's second worst-performing GameCube game in Japan.

[![Image 3: This screenshot shows the Helibokaan flying in a circular arena, attacking the barrier protecting Professor Isogashima. The game's interface displays the time, coin counter score, and Kururin with all three of his hearts remaining.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/1/17/Kururin_Squash_Boss_Fight_Screenshot.jpg/250px-Kururin_Squash_Boss_Fight_Screenshot.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kururin_Squash_Boss_Fight_Screenshot.jpg)

Kururin piloting the Helibokaan during the [boss fight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boss_(video_games) "Boss (video games)") against Professor Isogashima in the first world.

The player controls Kururin, a bird who pilots the Helirin, a constantly spinning helicopter, by navigating [mazes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maze "Maze") while avoiding walls and other obstacles. The player can hold down buttons on the [GameCube controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameCube_controller "GameCube controller") to adjust the speed at which the Helirin spins and the speed of the Helirin itself.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-HardcoreGaming101-3) Kururin has three hearts by default, and each stage contains checkpoints where their hearts can be refilled.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-NWR-4) If the player hits any obstacles, they lose a heart, and three seconds are added to the in-game timer, with the goal being to complete each stage in the least amount of time for a high score.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Manual-5) In the single-player mode, the player can select whether to control a larger or more compact Helirin, a method of adjusting difficulty.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-:0-6) Two modes are available from the start, the Adventure mode with the stages and story, as well as a Challenge mode where the player attempts to complete the stages as fast as possible.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Edge-7) After completing the Adventure mode, a third mode is unlocked where the player controls the center sphere of the Helirin, which does not feature the rotating helicopter blades, but can't stop moving.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-8) After completing this mode, the Extra mode is unlocked, featuring rotated versions of the stages.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-9)

_Kururin Squash!_ introduces new vehicles, enemies in stages, and [boss fights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boss_(video_games) "Boss (video games)") at the end of each world. The "Action Helirins" are helicopters that provide various advantages the standard Helirin does not. One of these vehicles is the Helibokaan,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-10) which is a helicopter that can break obstacles and punch enemies. The Helibashan can dive underwater to avoid obstacles on the surface, the Heliboboh can shoot fire when attached to rails, the Heliburuun can create whirlwinds, and the Helibibyuun can shoot objects using rapid fire.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-11)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Manual-5): 12–13  The single-player modes feature several unique worlds, with every few stages taking place in a new environment.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Nintendojo-12)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Manual-5): 28–29  Coins are present in every stage, and collecting all the coins will net the player a perfect bonus, increasing their total coin counter.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Euro-13) Coins can be used in shops, which contain many useful items and accessories. These items can increase the player's hearts, respawn them at the beginning after they lose their hearts, or provide a minimap for stages. The shop also contains movies that can guide the player on how to complete individual levels,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-HardcoreGaming101-3) with shops being run by members of the Magic Group, the false antagonists from _[Kururin Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin\_Paradise "Kururin Paradise")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-NWR-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Manual-5): 21

The multiplayer in _Kururin Squash!_ has two modes that support up to four players. The Race Mode has over forty obstacle courses where players attempt to reach the end while hitting opponents into walls or blocking their opponents' vehicles, taking place on stages from the Challenge mode.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Nintendojo-12) In the Battle Mode, players can fight on ten unique stages by using power-ups and weapons that is similar to [minigames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minigame "Minigame") from [_Super Monkey Ball_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Monkey_Ball_(video_game) "Super Monkey Ball (video game)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Nintendojo-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Cult_Classics-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Kikizo-15) The objective for this mode is to collect the most coins while attacking other players.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-NWR-4) By connecting a [GameCube – Game Boy Advance link cable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GameCube_%E2%80%93_Game_Boy_Advance_link_cable "GameCube – Game Boy Advance link cable"), up to four [Game Boy Advance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Boy_Advance "Game Boy Advance") systems can play a [spot the difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spot_the_difference "Spot the difference")-type quiz game, which can be purchased from the shop.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Kikizo-15)

[![Image 4: This screenshot depicts the ending cutscene for the first world, with Kururin rescuing his youngest siblings, Hyokorin and Loverin, from Professor Isogashima. The characters are illustrated on cardboard cutouts, which are held up by sticks extending to the bottom of the screen.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/3/3d/Kururin_Squash%21_Cutscene_Screenshot.png/250px-Kururin_Squash%21_Cutscene_Screenshot.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kururin_Squash!_Cutscene_Screenshot.png)

The story is told through a [paper puppet theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toy_theater "Toy theater") style, which received praise from critics.

After Kururin wins the lottery for his family, they travel across the four continents of the world. However, upon arriving back to their home in Kururin Village, only the parents of the family return. After losing track of his family members, Kururin goes on an adventure to find them across the four continents.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-:0-6)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Manual-5): 6–7  Throughout the journey, Kururin's guide, Teacher Hare, provides him with new Action Helirins that help him progress through the different worlds.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Manual-5): 12–13  Kururin travels to face Professor Isogashima, a mad inventor bird who has captured all the members of his family since they interfered with his research, and he releases them after being defeated in boss battles.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-:0-6)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-16) Professor Isogashima and his Isogashimachines serve as the main antagonists with the goal of making everyone else busy.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-17) Once Kururin returns home after rescuing his siblings, he discovers that his parents were also kidnapped by Professor Isogashima, so he travels to the fifth and final world in space to rescue them.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-18) When defeated, Professor Isogashima crash lands on their home planet, makes himself busy by fixing the problems caused by his Isogashimachines, and the Kururin family returns home.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-19)

_Kururin Squash!_ was developed by [Eighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eighting "Eighting"), and was the first game in the _Kururin_ series to transition from 2D to [3D computer graphics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_computer_graphics "3D computer graphics"). The directors and producers from _[Kururin Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin\_Paradise "Kururin Paradise")_ returned to work on _Kururin Squash!_ as the final entry in the series. [Yōichi Kotabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y%C5%8Dichi_Kotabe "Yōichi Kotabe") returns as the series' character designer, with it being the final game he serves that role at Nintendo prior to his departure from the company in 2007.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Credits-20) It was officially revealed in an issue of _[Famitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famitsu "Famitsu")_ magazine on August 5, 2004,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-21) and later released on October 14, 2004. It had a small advertising campaign, with a publication in a column of _[Nintendo Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo\_Dream "Nintendo Dream")_ and commercials that used the Helirin as a prop.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-22)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-23) In a developer interview with [Yuichi Toyama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuichi_Toyama "Yuichi Toyama") and Kenichi Yokoo for _[Sōkyūgurentai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terra\_Diver "Terra Diver")_ and _[Mahou Daisakusen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorcer\_Striker "Sorcer Striker")_, Yokoo cited _Kururin Squash!_ as his favorite non-arcade game he worked on.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-24) Eighting would later collaborate with Nintendo on the [Nintendo DS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_DS "Nintendo DS") game _[Master of Illusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master\_of\_Illusion\_(video\_game) "Master of Illusion (video game)")_ in 2006.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-25)

_Kururin Squash!_ received generally positive reviews,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-GameStats-31) with praise for the 3D visuals,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-NWR-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Cult_Classics-14) music,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-NWR-4)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Kikizo-15)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Nintendojo-12) as well as improved gameplay and controls from its predecessors.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Nintendojo-12)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-:0-6) The art style received praise, with colorful 3D environments and stylized cutscenes represented by cardboard puppets on sticks, creating a unique and refreshing style.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-NWRPrev-32)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-NWR-4)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Kikizo-15)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Nintendojo-12) The multiplayer modes were also complimented for their quality. Caleb Gossler of _Nintendojo_ claimed _Kururin Squash!_ to have "some of the best four-player party games on the GameCube".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Nintendojo-12) Chandra Nair of _[GamesTM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GamesTM "GamesTM")_ described the levels as "cunningly designed", complimenting them for taking advantage of the different abilities of the Action Helirins.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-GTM-27) Ben Kosmina of _Nintendo World Report_ described the overall experience as stellar, complimenting the title for having a low language barrier to enjoy the gameplay, despite its exclusivity to Japan.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-NWR-4) Similarly, Nadia Grace Mullings of _Game Rant_ claimed it to be "worthy of being one of the best GameCube titles, despite it having never been released in America".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-:1-33) Anoop Gantayat of _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ expressed interest in _Kururin Squash!_ releasing overseas due to the addictive gameplay, even if there were no plans to do so by [Nintendo of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_of_America "Nintendo of America").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-:0-6) The low price was also praised, with _[Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edge\_(magazine) "Edge (magazine)")_ magazine describing the price point as enticing.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-34)

The main criticism of _Kururin Squash!_ was its difficulty and short length. In comparison to the Game Boy Advance titles which featured more challenging stages, _Kururin Squash!_ contains generally easier levels that could be completed faster due to the improvement in movement accuracy, as a result of switching from a [d-pad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D-pad "D-pad") to the GameCube control stick.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-HardcoreGaming101-3)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-GTM-Mag-26)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Euro-13)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Edge-7) Despite this critique, others have claimed the difficulty level is still present. Jonti Davies of _Kikizo_ described the gameplay as "straightforward in principle, but, in later stages especially, often devilishly difficult in practice".[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Kikizo-15) Ollie Reynolds of _Nintendo Life_ shared this sentiment, noting how navigating the mazes can become "incredibly tense" as the player progresses.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-:2-35)_[Eurogamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurogamer "Eurogamer")_ later retracted this criticism, with Keza MacDonald stating that it hardly affects the overall experience, considering _Kururin Squash!_ a [cult classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_video_game "Cult video game") on the GameCube.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Cult_Classics-14) Additionally, critics were disappointed by the lack of multiplayer modes, in comparison to the multiple [minigames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minigame "Minigame") introduced in _Kururin Paradise_. Ben Kosmina of _Nintendo World Report_ considered the fewer number of multiplayer offerings disappointing.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-NWRPrev-32) Writers for _Edge_ magazine claimed the sixteen minigames from _Kururin Paradise_ were better than having only two in _Kururin Squash!_, with the Game Boy Advance link cable minigame being referred to as "no more than a novelty".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Edge-7) In retrospective reviews, _Kururin Squash!_ has been cited as one of the best Japanese-exclusive GameCube games,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-:1-33)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-36)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-37)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-Cult_Classics-14) with many desiring an English localization.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-38)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-:2-35)

In Japan, _Kururin Squash!_ reached the eighteenth position on sales charts during its initial launch week, selling 5,745 copies.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-39) It only placed among the top thirty weekly video game sales one additional time the following week.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-40)_Kururin Squash!_ sold a total of 18,562 copies in Japan from release to December 20, 2004.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-41) It was the third lowest-selling GameCube game in 2004 and the second lowest-selling first-party game behind [_Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternal_Darkness "Eternal Darkness"),[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-42) subsequently making it the lowest-selling entry in the _Kururin_ series, despite being sold at a budget price comparative to other GameCube titles.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-release-1)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-43)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kururin_Squash!#cite_note-44)

Description
-----------

After two adventures on the Game Boy Advance, Kururin goes 3D on the GameCube. In Kururin Squash!, you have to direct Kururin in his helicopter-like Heririn spinning stick through narrow mazes, while avoiding obstacles or courses' sides. The gameplay is spiced up with colourful backgrounds, bizarre enemies, weapons, and bounce pads that change the spin direction. When you get hit three times, the Heririn shatters.

The GameCube version introduces water levels with a submarine, guns, boxing gloves, twisters, flame-throwing, and boss battles. In the main puzzle mode, you have to collect loot and in the race mode, you have to finish the mazes within a target time. Multiplayer includes four-player split-screen frenzy and a battle mode where you have to collect coins while using the weapons to hold off your opponents.

**Kururin Squash!**[[Edit](https://nintendo.fandom.com/wiki/Kururin_Squash!?action=edit)][Talk]

_**Kururin Squash!**_ is a [GameCube](https://nintendo.fandom.com/wiki/Nintendo_GameCube "Nintendo GameCube") video game released by [Nintendo](https://nintendo.fandom.com/wiki/Nintendo "Nintendo") and [Eighting](https://nintendo.fandom.com/wiki/Eighting "Eighting") in [2004](https://nintendo.fandom.com/wiki/2004 "2004"). The game is a puzzle title released exclusively in Japan. In the game you control Kururin who is off to save all of his siblings after they went missing on a family trip across the four countries of the in-game world. 
Gameplay[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fnintendo.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FKururin_Squash%21%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Playing as Kururin, you go inside of a long rectangular ship that is constantly spinning. The ship, called a [Helirin](https://nintendo.fandom.com/wiki/Helirin "Helirin"), travels through maze-like buildings. If any part of the ship hits a wall three times, he'll have to start over. Your goal is to maneuver the ship in a way so that it doesn't hit any walls. Because it is constantly spinning, this will prove to be a challenge, though you can use this to your advantage as well when you are required to get through tight spaces that can only be entered when your ship is facing in a certain direction, though you must get through it fast incase it continues to spin and crash into the walls. There are three different speeds of the Helirin, and thankfully you can alter the speed to your liking.

Legacy[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fnintendo.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FKururin_Squash%21%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]
